selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What does the passage compare the whole world to?
questions.answer: It compares the world to a well-run kingdom or city.

questions.question: What are all things described as doing?
questions.answer: They are obeying and carrying out their own tasks.

questions.question: How are the parts of creation connected in the passage’s example?
questions.answer: They are connected like organized troops under command.

questions.question: What can happen when many hands try to do the same job?
questions.answer: Things get mixed up and confused.

questions.question: What is the result when many people try to control the same work?
questions.answer: The work becomes messy and mixed up.

questions.question: What do we really see in the universe instead?
questions.answer: We see harmony and order.

questions.question: Why is sharing rule against the honor of sovereignty?
questions.answer: Because true kingship does not accept a rival.

questions.question: What human weakness is mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: People may fight cruelly for a small, temporary rule.

questions.question: What does that teach us about Allah’s sovereignty?
questions.answer: His sovereignty is far greater and never shared.

questions.question: What title is given to this part of the passage?
questions.answer: It is about sovereignty.

questions.question: What picture is used to help explain this idea?
questions.answer: The picture of a kingdom or a city under strong rule.

questions.question: Why are atoms, plants, animals, and stars all mentioned together?
questions.answer: To show that Allah’s rule covers everything.

questions.question: What do these many ordered groups point to?
questions.answer: They point to one complete authority over all.

questions.question: Why would more than one god not fit with that order?
questions.answer: Because shared control would bring disorder.

questions.question: What do we see instead of ruin?
questions.answer: We see careful order everywhere.

questions.question: Where does the passage say this order can be seen?
questions.answer: In very tiny things and in huge things too.

questions.question: Why is rivalry not accepted in sovereignty?
questions.answer: Because rulership has greatness and does not share its place.

questions.question: How does the example of humans fighting for small power strengthen the message?
questions.answer: It makes it easier to understand that Allah’s perfect rule cannot be shared.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the universe when looked at with care?
questions.answer: As active, successful, and wisely managed.

questions.question: What does a careful person see in the universe?
questions.answer: A world run with wisdom and firmness.

questions.question: Why does the passage say partners cannot share Allah’s rule?
questions.answer: Because one rule over all things cannot be shared without harm.

questions.question: What do these ordered “armies” show about Allah?
questions.answer: That His authority reaches everything.

questions.question: What simple everyday idea is used to explain this?
questions.answer: One place cannot be run well by two top leaders.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention people wanting power?
questions.answer: To show that even weak humans do not like to share rule.
